1.pericope_label: Hear ye this, O priests; and hearken, ye house of Israel; and give ye ear, O house of the king; for judgment is toward you
debates: Whether the priests summoned are lawful priests, the priests of the calves, or princes
What the clause about judgment means
Where the two places named lie and why they carry the figure of snare and net
outliers: Calvin sets aside the reading that makes the verse a rebuke for maladministration, treating it instead as a citation to the tribunal of God
Wesley locates the first of the two places in Libanus, where Clarke and Ellicott both put it beyond the Jordan in Gilead
themes: A process instituted, with defendants called to appear and answer
A snare set on one mountain and a net spread upon another
Priests of the calves standing beside priests of the tribe of Levi
Rank that cannot keep out wrath because it did not keep out sin

2.pericope_label: And the revolters are profound to make slaughter, though I have been a rebuker of them all
debates: What being profound to make slaughter means
How the last clause of the accusation should be rendered
Whether Ephraim and Israel name the same body or two
outliers: Ellicott abandons the hunting figure the others all keep, reading the clause as a statement that the apostates have gone deep in iniquity
Keil and Delitzsch deny that the two mountains were places of idolatrous sacrifice, which the other voices assume
themes: Hunters flat on the ground to work their snares, and pits lightly covered over
Sacrificing called killing, as a temple might be called the shambles
Excuses that cannot dazzle eyes which see through them
A demon of whoredom seated in the heart, from which the works emanate

4.pericope_label: And the pride of Israel doth testify to his face: therefore shall Israel and Ephraim fall in their iniquity
debates: Whether their doings will not let them turn or they will not frame their doings to turn
Whether the pride testifies against them or is itself humbled
What the pride of Israel names
outliers: Keil and Delitzsch reject the reading drawn from the Greek on the ground that it cannot be reconciled with the phrase that follows, where Calvin allows it as not unsuitable before setting it aside
Ellicott dates the chapter later than the oracle before it because the drawing in of Judah is a new note
themes: Doings that will not let a man turn, and a will with no will to good
An obstinacy sunk as into a deep gulf, like the abyss
Pride called as the only witness needed for a conviction
Satiety that begets ferocity in a prosperous people

6.pericope_label: They shall go with their flocks and with their herds to seek the Lord; but they shall not find him; he hath withdrawn himself from them
debates: Why a multitude of sacrifices fails to find the Lord
What the strange children are
What the month is that shall devour them
outliers: Calvin rejects both the intermarriage reading and the bad-upbringing reading of the strange children, holding that the point is a corruption reaching the next generation and past recovery
Clarke reports a rendering that replaces the month with the locust, and Wesley refers it to a usurpation that lasted a month, where Ellicott makes it a personified period of invasion
themes: Flocks and herds brought as though a whole substance were driven to the altar
A husband withdrawn from a wife who has been unfaithful
Children infected with the vices of their parents, leaving no hope for the posterity
A horn and a trumpet blown to warn a land already invaded

8.pericope_label: Blow ye the cornet in Gibeah, and the trumpet in Ramah: cry aloud at Beth-aven, after thee, O Benjamin
debates: Whether the two places named lie in one kingdom or in both
What the cry after Benjamin means
Who is being told to blow the alarm
outliers: Wesley reads the cry as coming after the cries of others, calling Benjamin to join in lamenting, where the rest hear the enemy at his back
Ellicott alone infers from the sightline of the two hills that the peril to the unnamed capital is what the verse is really disclosing
themes: A bent animal horn and a long straight metal trumpet sounded together
A herald sent through a whole kingdom to proclaim war
A cup of trembling going round from tribe to tribe
A controversy that was a trial at law becoming a trial by battle

9.pericope_label: The princes of Judah were like them that remove the bound: therefore I will pour out my wrath upon them like water
debates: Whether the desolation threatened is temporary or lasting
Whether the princes are compared to boundary-movers or actually were such
What boundary is meant by the figure
outliers: Calvin takes the removed boundary for the whole political order, and then for the limit that had kept one tribe separate as the heritage of God
Gill reports interpreters who read the particle as a note of certainty rather than of comparison, so that the princes did the thing itself
themes: A landmark quietly shifted in the dark by men with no regard to right
Walls of right scaled and the enclosure of law leapt over
Paternal corrections laid aside as remedies applied in vain
Wrath poured out like water, in fuller force on the leaders than on the people

11.pericope_label: Therefore will I be unto Ephraim as a moth, and to the house of Judah as rottenness
debates: What the rare word rendered commandment means
Who is to blame when a king imposes a false worship
Whether the second figure is a worm or a rotting disease
outliers: Ellicott gives weight to the Greek reading vanities, from a different Hebrew word, against the majority who take the word for an ordinance of the king
Calvin refuses the excuse that the change of religion was the act of one man, holding the alacrity of the people to be proof of their perfidy
themes: A moth feeding privately in a garment until it is of no use
Rottenness working unseen and showing itself too late
A thorn in the conscience sharpened by the preaching of the law
Judgment that corrodes slowly where an earlier judgment came like a deluge

13.pericope_label: For I will be unto Ephraim as a lion, and as a young lion to the house of Judah: I, even I, will tear and go away
debates: Whether the name of the king sent to is a proper name or a description
Which Assyrian ruler is meant
Why the figure changes from a moth to a lion
outliers: Ellicott sets out at length the case that the name is an appellative meaning contention rather than the name of any king in the Assyrian lists, and leaves the identification unsettled
Gill carries the two beasts past Assyria and Babylon to the Romans, where the others stop with the Assyrian invasion
themes: A sick man who feels the pain and never asks how he came by it
A physician sought from the very power that inflicted the wound
A moth and a worm laid aside for a lion with an open mouth
A lion that carries off its prey and withdraws to its own place

15.pericope_label: I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face
debates: How God can be said to go away and return to his place
Whether the last verb means to seek early or simply to seek
Whether the withdrawal ends in restoration
outliers: Clarke reads the abandonment as already answered, since the chapter following records the repentance it was meant to produce, and calls these verses instances of the true sublime
Calvin declines the sense of seeking early that the word properly carries, preferring the plainer sense of seeking
themes: A God who shuts himself up as though he had no more concern for a people
A face hidden only as far as the outward condition of a nation shows it
Speech accommodated to the perceptions of men
A prodigal in the flush of a new morning arising to go to the Father
